package com.gymie.workout.infrastructure.presentation.web.converters

import com.gymie.workout.core.domain.workout.SetWeight
import com.gymie.workout.core.exceptions.WorkoutValidationException
import com.gymie.workout.infrastructure.presentation.web.dto.SetWeightDto

/**
 * The single place [SetWeightDto] (the wire shape) and [SetWeight] (the domain type) meet — and
 * therefore the single place the wire shape's rule is stated: `kind` is one of the two known
 * constants, and `value` is present exactly when `kind` is `MEASURED`.
 *
 * Both writers of a set's weight go through here — the whole-workout `POST`/`PUT` via
 * `WorkoutRequestValidator` and `WorkoutWebConverters`, and `PATCH /{id}/sets/{setId}` via the
 * controller — so neither can accept a shape the other refuses. Every refusal is a
 * [WorkoutValidationException], which this module's own `WorkoutExceptionHandler` maps to `400`;
 * a bare `IllegalArgumentException` here would leave `:workout`'s input contract depending on an
 * unscoped advice in an unrelated module, and would surface as a `500` in a controller slice.
 *
 * No unit crosses here in either direction: a set carries a number, its workout carries the unit.
 * Nothing converts a number, so a weight is stored, and read back, as the one the user typed.
 */
object SetWeightWebConverter {
    fun toDomain(dto: SetWeightDto?): SetWeight? =
        when (dto?.kind) {
            null -> null
            SetWeightDto.KIND_BODYWEIGHT -> bodyweight(dto)
            SetWeightDto.KIND_MEASURED -> measured(dto)
            else -> throw WorkoutValidationException("Weight kind must be MEASURED or BW")
        }

    private fun bodyweight(dto: SetWeightDto): SetWeight {
        if (dto.value != null) throw WorkoutValidationException("A BW weight must not carry a value")
        return SetWeight.Bodyweight
    }

    private fun measured(dto: SetWeightDto): SetWeight {
        val value = dto.value ?: throw WorkoutValidationException("A MEASURED weight requires a value")
        return SetWeight.Measured(value)
    }

    fun toDto(weight: SetWeight?): SetWeightDto? =
        when (weight) {
            null -> null
            is SetWeight.Bodyweight -> SetWeightDto(kind = SetWeightDto.KIND_BODYWEIGHT)
            is SetWeight.Measured -> SetWeightDto(kind = SetWeightDto.KIND_MEASURED, value = weight.value)
        }
}

package com.gymie.workout.infrastructure.presentation.web.converters

import com.gymie.workout.core.domain.workout.SetEffort
import com.gymie.workout.core.exceptions.WorkoutValidationException
import com.gymie.workout.infrastructure.presentation.web.dto.SetEffortDto

/**
 * The single place [SetEffortDto] (the wire shape) and [SetEffort] (the domain type) meet — and
 * therefore the single place the wire shape's rule is stated: `kind` is one of the two known
 * constants, and `value` is present exactly when `kind` is `COUNT`.
 *
 * Both writers of a set's effort go through here — the whole-workout `POST`/`PUT` via
 * `WorkoutRequestValidator` and `WorkoutWebConverters`, and `PATCH /{id}/sets/{setId}` via the
 * controller — so neither can accept a shape the other refuses. Every refusal is a
 * [WorkoutValidationException], which this module's own `WorkoutExceptionHandler` maps to `400`;
 * a bare `IllegalArgumentException` here would leave `:workout`'s input contract depending on an
 * unscoped advice in an unrelated module, and would surface as a `500` in a controller slice.
 *
 * The persistence sentinel for [SetEffort.Max] never appears here in either direction: `MAX` is a
 * `kind` on the wire, so a numeric `-1` is a count of minus one and is refused as such by
 * `SetValueSpecification`.
 */
object SetEffortWebConverter {
    fun toDomain(dto: SetEffortDto?): SetEffort? =
        when (dto?.kind) {
            null -> null
            SetEffortDto.KIND_MAX -> max(dto)
            SetEffortDto.KIND_COUNT -> count(dto)
            else -> throw WorkoutValidationException("Effort kind must be COUNT or MAX")
        }

    private fun max(dto: SetEffortDto): SetEffort {
        if (dto.value != null) throw WorkoutValidationException("A MAX effort value must not carry a count")
        return SetEffort.Max
    }

    private fun count(dto: SetEffortDto): SetEffort {
        val value = dto.value ?: throw WorkoutValidationException("A COUNT effort value requires a count")
        return SetEffort.Count(value)
    }

    fun toDto(effort: SetEffort?): SetEffortDto? =
        when (effort) {
            null -> null
            is SetEffort.Max -> SetEffortDto(kind = SetEffortDto.KIND_MAX)
            is SetEffort.Count -> SetEffortDto(kind = SetEffortDto.KIND_COUNT, value = effort.value)
        }
}

import com.gymie.workout.core.domain.workout.SetWeight
import com.gymie.workout.core.exceptions.WorkoutValidationException
import com.gymie.workout.infrastructure.presentation.web.dto.SetWeightDto

/**
 * The single place [SetWeightDto] (the wire shape) and [SetWeight] (the domain type) meet — and
 * therefore the single place the wire shape's rule is stated: `kind` is one of the two known
 * constants, and `value` is present exactly when `kind` is `MEASURED`.
 *
 * Both writers of a set's weight go through here — the whole-workout `POST`/`PUT` via
 * `WorkoutRequestValidator` and `WorkoutWebConverters`, and `PATCH /{id}/sets/{setId}` via the
 * controller — so neither can accept a shape the other refuses. Every refusal is a
 * [WorkoutValidationException], which this module's own `WorkoutExceptionHandler` maps to `400`;
 * a bare `IllegalArgumentException` here would leave `:workout`'s input contract depending on an
 * unscoped advice in an unrelated module, and would surface as a `500` in a controller slice.
 *
 * No unit crosses here in either direction: a set carries a number, its workout carries the unit.
 * Nothing converts a number, so a weight is stored, and read back, as the one the user typed.
 */
object SetWeightWebConverter {
    fun toDomain(dto: SetWeightDto?): SetWeight? =
        when (dto?.kind) {
            null -> null
            SetWeightDto.KIND_BODYWEIGHT -> bodyweight(dto)
            SetWeightDto.KIND_MEASURED -> measured(dto)
            else -> throw WorkoutValidationException("Weight kind must be MEASURED or BW")
        }

    private fun bodyweight(dto: SetWeightDto): SetWeight {
        if (dto.value != null) throw WorkoutValidationException("A BW weight must not carry a value")
        return SetWeight.Bodyweight
    }

    private fun measured(dto: SetWeightDto): SetWeight {
        val value = dto.value ?: throw WorkoutValidationException("A MEASURED weight requires a value")
        return SetWeight.Measured(value)
    }

    fun toDto(weight: SetWeight?): SetWeightDto? =
        when (weight) {
            null -> null
            is SetWeight.Bodyweight -> SetWeightDto(kind = SetWeightDto.KIND_BODYWEIGHT)
            is SetWeight.Measured -> SetWeightDto(kind = SetWeightDto.KIND_MEASURED, value = weight.value)
        }
}

}

)
